source.title: EARL: Embracing amnesic replay for learning with noisy labels
source.authors: Monica Millunzi; Lorenzo Bonicelli; A. Porrello; Jacopo Credi; Petter N. Kolm; Simone Calderara

record.file_problem: The supplied full text is titled “May the Forgetting Be with You: Alternate Replay for Learning with Noisy Labels,” while the metadata title is “EARL: Embracing amnesic replay for learning with noisy labels.” The text itself is complete.
record.tranche_reason: Builds a continual-learning method on the small-loss and forgetting effects for identifying noisy examples, but does not test the listed random-label fitting claims.
record.gate_note: The study reports noisy-label learning and accuracy results, but does not report random-label training error, chance-level test error, fitting time across corruption rates, or the other behaviors named in V1–V6. Its main accuracy comparisons evaluate the authors’ proposed method and baselines, not the listed claim’s behavior. Figure 1’s clean/noisy loss comparison is background motivation from a rehearsal baseline; the study does not state numeric values for it.
record.test_reason: The study uses the early-learning/small-loss premise to design a noisy-label continual-learning method. Its experiments measure method accuracy, buffer quality, forgetting, and mitigation of noisy-sample learning. They do not establish any listed version: Figure A lacks a clean-sample learning comparison, and Figure 1 concerns loss separation during replay and induced forgetting rather than the initial ordering of signal learning and noise memorization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that AER maintains clean/noisy loss separation and ABS balances buffer purity and diversity, improving noisy-label continual learning.
record.recipe_differences: Continual class-incremental learning with noisy labels; alternates replay and forgetting and uses asymmetric buffer sampling. It does not reproduce the original random-label experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: AER changes the reported rate at which noisy current-task samples are learned.

fits_no_version.finding: On the second Split CIFAR-10 task, AER slows convergence on noisy current-task samples; FAA is 28.74% with AER versus 27.35% without it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alternating replay and forgetting can slow noisy-current-task learning and improve continual-learning accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 1 reports that ordinary replay makes clean and noisy buffer losses indistinguishable, whereas alternating replay and forgetting maintains separation, with noisy losses increasing when replay stops.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induced forgetting can restore clean/noisy buffer-loss separation during continual learning.

record.problems: The result relevant to noisy-sample learning is shown in a figure, without numeric loss-curve values or uncertainty. The study's setting is continual class-incremental learning and does not measure random-label fitting as defined in the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: Main FAA tables and comparisons, including the authors’ method and its baselines, were left out because they report continual-learning accuracy rather than the behavior named by V1–V6. Figure 1’s clean/noisy loss comparison is cited as motivation and has no extracted numeric outcome for the listed versions.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Time to fit true versus random labels and convergence time as corruption increases. Method runtime comparisons do not measure these.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit alongside steadily deteriorating test performance across the full corruption range. FAA at selected noise rates alone does not establish this conjunction.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting, and generalization after removing these regularizers.
Initial learning of shared real-data patterns before noisy-label memorization. Replay-related loss separation and slowing noisy-sample learning do not establish that ordering.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 1 is an original experiment, not merely a cited motivational result, although its measured behavior does not establish V6's initial learning order. The supplied text is the 2024 arXiv manuscript with a different title from the DOI metadata; these verdicts apply to the supplied manuscript.

versions.untested_parts: Random labeling of the training set, zero or near-zero training error, chance-level test error, and unchanged architecture or training hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and convergence as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily rising test error across corruption rates.
Whether weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation prevent random-label fitting or are necessary for true-label generalization.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy or random labels under ordinary training.

rows.subject: ER-ACE
rows.operation_detail: Compared training with AER against training without AER; the plotted measure is loss on noisy samples from the current task.
rows.measure: Rate of learning noisy samples; Final Average Accuracy
rows.note: The authors state that AER vastly reduces the convergence rate of noisy samples and improves FAA over the baseline. Figure A gives FAA values of 28.74% with AER and 27.35% without AER, but the loss-curve values are figure only. This result concerns noisy-sample learning in continual learning, not one of V1–V6.
rows.check: The reported AER effect is observed, but this comparison cannot determine a claim-version effect. It combines two measures and should be split: noisy-current-task loss trajectories and FAA. FAA is 28.74% with AER versus 27.35% without AER; loss-curve values are not recoverable from the supplied text. Neither measure establishes clean-before-noisy learning, relative true/random fitting time, or complete random-label fitting.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
